- **Every hook runs through one launcher.** A hook command string is parsed by whichever shell the harness picked, and `bash` on Windows often names the WSL stub, which cannot run these handlers — so a guard or gate reported a failed hook and no verdict. All commands are now `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.py" plugin|repo <handler.sh>`: the launcher locates a real Git Bash, puts its toolchain on the child's PATH, resolves the handler under the plugin or the checkout, and forwards stdin and the exit code; native contract gate rule J refuses any other command shape. The no-`jq` envelope reader now tolerates whitespace too, which silently blanked every field on a pretty-printed envelope.

- **The plugin is one native tree for every supported harness — no generator, no mirror.** Each harness discovers the same committed files through its own plugin mechanism (`.claude-plugin/` and `.codex-plugin/` manifests, shared `hooks/hooks.json`, shared `.mcp.json`, agent stubs copied unchanged), so a skill edit ships once and needs no regeneration step. `codex-sync/`, the drift gate, and the synced harness copy of `provider.sh` are gone; hook provider behavior now lives in one adapter per harness under `hooks/lib/providers/<id>.sh`. Harness-agnosticism is a standing requirement from now on: `CLAUDE.md` carries the rule, `PROVIDERS.md` carries the supported-harness registry, `CAPABILITIES.md` carries the capability matrix, `providers/CONFORMANCE.md` carries live proof plus the add-a-harness checklist, and `hooks/native-contract-gate.sh` blocks (Stop and commit) on harness vocabulary in skill prose, unsupported frontmatter, manifest/registry drift, a tracked generated mirror, or a missing adapter fixture.

- **Gates no longer tax interactive work.** A turn that only talked now costs one short-circuit check instead of the whole suite, and the three expensive code gates (`maven-compile`, `java-format`, `ui-lint`) moved off Stop onto a **`pre-commit`** git hook — same enforcement, paid once per commit instead of once per question. What made this necessary: gate latency on Windows/git-bash is **subprocess count**, not algorithm (MSYS fork emulation runs ~0.5–2s per spawn against ~20–40ms native, and degrades under load), and the suite was spawning hundreds — a cache key that re-hashed the tree with two forks per changed file, recomputed independently by all seven gates; a registry gate re-grepping the same files once per skill and once per env var; a wiring gate running a full-monorepo scan **per new file**. Now: one Stop hook (`stop-gates.sh`) deriving the change set once (`gate-context.sh`) and entering a gate only when the change set holds a path it could possibly gate; per-gate pass caches keyed on **that gate's own inputs**, so editing a spec file no longer re-runs the plugin-registry gates; one batched repo scan for every wiring candidate; one `awk` pass for genericity whatever the diff's size. Measured on the same tree: full cold Stop 56–95s (was over 2min, with the genericity gate alone recorded at 12min), unchanged tree 7.5–12.5s, and design-chain artifacts (PRD/SDD/plan/ADR/journal files) no longer report as wiring orphans — they have no textual referrer by construction. Also fixed: two registry-gate false blocks (Windows Python's CRLF broke every `plugin.json` membership match; the gate flagged a variable named inside its own trailing comment). New env toggles `AFK_GATE_CTX_DISABLE`, `AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES`, `AFK_MAVEN_LOCK_WAIT`. **Restart the session** (hooks.json changed), and run a session in each existing checkout so `install-git-hooks.sh` adds the `pre-commit` hook. Cost model + the rules a new gate must follow: `hooks/README.md`.

- The afk plugin now carries the **whole gate suite** — the four gates that previously required the separate, rarely-installed `payable-harness` plugin (`java-rules-gate` CSJ code standards, `i18n-parity-gate` locale parity, `crowdstrike-guard`, `explore-counter`) are registered in this plugin's `hooks.json`, invoked in place from `tools/payable/ai-agents/harness/hooks/` so they track the checkout, not the plugin snapshot. The `payable-harness` plugin is **retired** (manifests + its `hooks.json` deleted; uninstall any old copy) — enabling `afk-toolkit@afk-toolkit` is the single opt-in. Notably this closes the gap where CSJ001 (no inline FQNs in Java) was documented and machine-checked but silently unenforced. `/reload-plugins` to pick it up.

claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to SessionStart over the name forms this pass searched

Both hooks files register one SessionStart group, matcher *, of 3 handlers run through run-hook.py --soft: install-git-hooks.sh --quiet (timeout 15), update-notice.sh (timeout 15) and repo-list SessionStart (timeout 60); the files differ only in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} versus ${PLUGIN_ROOT}.

Claude Code loads hooks/hooks.json by its default path (.claude-plugin/plugin.json names no hooks key; probe debug log at providers/CONFORMANCE.md:320); Codex loads hooks/hooks.codex.json through .codex-plugin/plugin.json:53.

run-hook.py's plugin kind runs hooks/<name>.sh with the harness's stdin, stdout and whole environment plus AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT, applies no event-source or session filter, exits 0 on an absent handler, and returns 0 under --soft; so a new handler sees the envelope on stdin and any launch-only environment value, and its stdout goes straight to the harness.

repo-list SessionStart runs the repository's .afk/hooks.json SessionStart entries with the envelope on stdin; on SessionStart a fault goes to stderr only and the exit is 0, which scripts/tests/test_run_hook.py:113-120 pins.

The harness is the only reader of SessionStart output: in a Claude Code pane agent the agent quoted two probe nonces from its start context, outputs arrived in finish order, and a 23.9 KB output became a saved-file preview; no plugin code reads handler output. update-notice.sh prints plain stdout.
In a Claude Code pane agent SessionStart fires at startup, resume, compact (after a PreCompact mark) and clear (new session id), and no SessionStart mark appeared at any of 11 subagent starts.

In a Codex CLI pane agent SessionStart fires at startup, resume and clear; after /compact the screen showed no SessionStart line; delivery of output to the agent is unproven because the probe granted no trust entry for a printing handler.

The Claude envelope carries source (fixture value startup; probe values startup, resume, compact, clear); the Codex fixture carries no source; afk_hook_field prints an empty string for an absent key; no existing handler or test reads source (3 accessor hits, none for source).

The source test has to live inside the handler: native-contract-gate rule E refuses any hooks/hooks.json matcher outside CAPABILITIES.md:28, which has no compact token, so the new entry goes in the * group.

A new entry `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.py" --soft plugin <name>.sh` passes native-contract-gate rules E and J, and rule I passes for an LF script, which .gitattributes:5 enforces; the gate reads only hooks/hooks.json, never hooks/hooks.codex.json.

hooks/tests/hook-smoke.sh:227-243 is the only test that pins both registrations: it fails unless the two hooks files are equal modulo the root variable, so the handler must be appended to both identically. No CI job runs hook-smoke.sh (.github/workflows/ holds only release-gate.yml); README.md:324 lists it in the manual dev loop.

providers/PARITY.md:103 says the native-contract gate diffs hooks.codex.json against its twin; the code refutes it: the gate reads only hooks/hooks.json (native-contract-gate.sh:226) and the twin diff lives in hooks/tests/hook-smoke.sh:243.

CAPABILITIES.md:33 and hooks/README.md:19 write the command form as `plugin|repo <handler.sh>`; the launcher's kinds are `plugin <handler.sh>` and `repo-list <event>` (run-hook.py:295, native-contract-gate.sh:263-267).

Codex keys hook trust as <marketplace>:hooks/hooks.codex.json:<event>:<group>:<index> with a hash of the definition as the value, so appending the handler at index 3 of the SessionStart group adds one key and leaves the 3 existing keys and hashes unchanged (inferred from the key form); the new definition needs a human trust grant, and setup probe O4 reports it untrusted until then; inserting it before an existing entry would shift that entry's index (inferred).

skill-registry-gate check C blocks the Stop gate when a hooks/*.sh reads an all-caps variable assigned nowhere in hooks/ and absent from skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md, so the launch-only value needs an E-table row in the same change.

A value in the pane agent's process environment reaches a SessionStart handler: run-hook.py passes os.environ down, and a herdr pane --env value reached Stop hook processes on both harnesses; that it reaches SessionStart hook processes is inferred from the same parent process, not observed.

No code outside docs/ names agent-start or a charter (case-blind search, 0 hits), so nothing sets the launch-only value today and the new handler is silent in every session until agent-start ships it.
